text:
Ethan: Hi folks, first day on Windows 11 (work laptop). Following the onboarding guide but hitting issues: asdf install for python/node fails inside WSL2 with `pyenv: no such file or directory` and npm native modules fail to compile. Also devcontainer builds in VS Code time out. Anyone with WSL2 + asdf tips?

Riya: Welcome! :wave: Two quick things: 1) are you running asdf inside WSL (Ubuntu) or in Windows powershell? asdf should live in WSL shell not Windows for repo work. 2) For WSL devcontainers, make sure Docker Desktop has WSL integration enabled (Settings -> Resources -> WSL Integration).

Ethan: Using Ubuntu 22.04 in WSL. I installed asdf via the Linux instructions and added `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` to `~/.bashrc`. `asdf plugin-list` shows nodejs and python but `asdf install python 3.11.4` bails early: `pyenv: /home/ethan/.asdf/plugins/python/bin/python-build: line 50: pyenv: command not found`.

Riya: That sounds like the python plugin expecting pyenv helpers. Try reinstalling the plugin per our notes: `asdf plugin-remove python && asdf plugin-add python` then ensure `git` submodules are updated: `cd ~/.asdf/plugins/python && git submodule update --init --recursive`. Also install build deps: `sudo apt-get install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libreadline-dev libbz2-dev libsqlite3-dev`.

Ethan: Ran those, build proceeds further but `node-gyp` fails during npm install of native deps: `gyp ERR! stack Error: Can't find Python executable "python2"`. On Ubuntu python2 isn't installed.

Riya: node-gyp historically required python2; newer versions use python3. Install `python-is-python3` or create a symlink: `sudo apt install python-is-python3` or `sudo ln -s $(which python3) /usr/bin/python2` (not ideal). Also ensure `npm` uses the asdf-installed node binary (run `which node` inside WSL).

Ethan: That fixed node-gyp. VS Code Remote - WSL devcontainer still errors with `timeout waiting for server` when building image. Logs show Docker context can't access `/mnt/c/Users` files.

IT Support: For Docker/WSL file permission oddities, prefer cloning your repo inside the WSL filesystem (e.g., ~/projects) not under /mnt/c. Windows-hosted files are slower and can timeout. Move the repo into WSL ext4 and rebuild devcontainer.

Ethan: Moved repo, rebuilt container, success. Two last asks: 1) my git user signing with gpg doesn't work in WSL; 2) how to persist SSH agent across WSL sessions?

Riya: For gpg, either run gpg inside WSL and import your key (use `gpg --import`) or use the Windows gpg agent via the gpg-agent socket forwarded into WSL (advanced). We usually recommend importing keys into WSL to keep workflows simple. For SSH agent persistence, add `eval $(ssh-agent -s) && ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to `~/.bash_profile` or use the Windows OpenSSH agent forwarded into WSL by enabling `ForwardAgent` in your `~/.ssh/config` and using the `wsl-ssh-agent` helper.

Ethan: Imported keys and added ssh-agent start to my profile. All green now. Thanks for the rapid help!

Devex Bot: Welcome aboard Ethan! Quick checklist reminder: for WSL onboarding we recommend: clone into WSL fs, install build-essentials, asdf plugins, enable Docker WSL integration, and add `~/.asdf/.tool-versions` to your dotfiles. See https://redwood.ai/devex/wsl for docs.
